3 follow ups that win the job back, without being pushy. Swipe ▸

slides.title: Day 2: make yes *easy*
slides.body: No reply is not always a no. People get busy. Resend the job and the price, and offer one real time. SAMPLE: “Hi Dana, still happy to repaint the 2 bedrooms for $1,200. I have Thursday at 8 AM open. Want me to hold it?”

slides.title: Day 5: ask what is *in the way*
slides.body: Price is not always the reason. Ask if anything on the quote is unclear, or offer a smaller option. SAMPLE: “Any questions on the quote? I could also do just the main bedroom for $650.”

slides.title: Last one: *close the loop*
slides.body: Low pressure, door open. No guilt, no fake deadline. SAMPLE: “I will close this out for now so I stop filling your phone. Just reply if you want to book later.”

slides.title: Then *stop*
slides.body: Two or three follow ups is plenty. After that, move on. Keep their details and check in next season instead of chasing every week.

slides.title: *Claude* drafts it
slides.body: Paste into Claude (the free plan works): I sent [name] a quote for [service] at [price] on [day], no reply in [days] days. Write one short, friendly follow up in my voice: [paste 2 texts I sent]. Say if it is the 1st, 2nd or last. Offer one next step. Do not invent discounts.
